partner_context.their_ambition: You are Europe's leading taxi and mobility platform — 180+ cities across nine countries — now part of Lyft's European expansion while retaining a distinct multi-country taxi network.
partner_context.their_pressure: European urban taxi demand is mature; growth needs premium tiers and multimodal surfaces that bypass road congestion — especially on coasts, islands, and harbour cities.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the foiling water supply layer for FREENOW's coastal and island corridors: Greece, Italy, France, Spain, the UK and Ireland — booked in-app on existing registry geometry.

hero.title: FREENOW × Navier — Europe's taxi platform, on the water
hero.subtitle: Mediterranean islands, Riviera coasts, and Thames harbour runs — the surface no taxi app owns yet.
hero.what_we_do_together: We add a foiling water tier across FREENOW's densest European coastal corridors — Greek islands, Italian archipelagos, the Côte d'Azur, Balearics, and the Thames — on registry geometry that is already display-ready.

why_now: Foiling lifts the hull clear of the water: faster, dramatically more efficient per passenger-mile, smooth and near-silent, hybrid-capable with no charging-infrastructure dependency, and autonomy-ready. A ~100-vessel network is already ramping in the Maldives (WSJ/Bloomberg, 2026), and coastal regulators are mandating clean harbour craft. The category gets claimed cluster-by-cluster.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water — roughly 10× more efficient than a conventional hull, faster, smoother, and quiet — with a software-defined fleet that keeps improving over time.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier uses the oceans and berths that already exist. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Coastal ride demand is dense, ferry corridors are slow and weather-exposed, and the water surface is still unowned by any mobility platform.

multimodal_fit: FREENOW already dispatches taxis and multimodal trips across Europe. A foiling pier is the water leg in the same trip graph — taxi to the marina, foil across the bay, taxi on arrival.

differentiation.why_navier: A uniform software-defined foiling fleet across nine countries — the premium water tier Lyft's European platform can light up market by market without new infrastructure.

proof_points.claim: The network model is real and already at scale.
proof_points.evidence: A ~100-vessel foiling network is ramping in the Maldives — the premium tier FREENOW can light up market by market.

proof_points.claim: The route universe is grounded in existing geometry.
proof_points.evidence: Thirty of FREENOW's registry cities across six countries already carry Atlas coastal geometry.

proof_points.claim: The water tier needs no new infrastructure.
proof_points.evidence: A uniform software-defined foiling fleet is hybrid-capable with no charging dependency and uses existing harbours.

network_thesis.headline: The water layer of Europe's leading taxi platform.
network_thesis.body: FREENOW operates in 180+ European cities; thirty inherited registry cities already have Atlas coastal geometry. Each is a ready foiling corridor — island hops, Riviera runs, and harbour commutes inside the app riders already use.
network_thesis.how_to_read: Each card is a country coastal cluster. Start in Greece or the Côte d'Azur.
network_thesis.coverage_note: FREENOW spans nine European countries; these thirty inherited registry cities are the first exact-bound coastal footprint from the 80-20 inheritance pass.

revenue_potential.headline: The floor and the prize — every rung traces to grounded, sourced demand.
revenue_potential.modal_lead: We start from grounded corridor demand. Each step adds one realistic expansion lever — network width, induced demand, journey wallet, platform take.
revenue_potential.anchor_note: $11M/yr premium sea-transfer spend on sourced corridors today — the anchor every rung builds from.

whose_money_legend.navier_transport_revenue: Fare the Navier boats collect. This is the corridor P&L (atom.py). SOM/SAM rungs are in this unit.
whose_money_legend.journey_gmv: Total spend on the whole island journey flowing through the super-app: transport + food + stays + experiences + ads + parcel/logistics. Gross, all merchants. TAM rung is in this unit.
whose_money_legend.platform_take: The partner's (Grab's) own commission revenue on journey_gmv. Derived line — this is the number that makes a super-app care, not the boat fare.

revenue_potential.cite_rule: Cite MID. 'High' stacks every optimistic assumption — ceiling, not headline.

rungs.label: SOM — floor (published)
rungs.basis: sourced flagship corridors · 10% capture · today's demand

rungs.label: SOM — full network
rungs.basis: whole mapped network · 10% capture · today's demand (no growth assumed)

rungs.label: SAM — matured network
rungs.basis: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market · leading-operator 25% capture, network-wide

rungs.label: Marine mobility TAM — induced marine-transfer market
rungs.basis: SAM divided by leading-operator capture — the full inducible water-transfer wallet at network maturity

rungs.label: Journey GMV — food + stays + experiences (≈3× TAM)
rungs.basis: add food, stays, and experiences to every crossing in the induced market

rungs.label: Partner platform revenue on Navier
rungs.basis: platform commission on journey GMV routed through the Navier network (subset of full Journey GMV)

ladder_transitions.headline: Same 10% capture, expanded to the full mapped network
ladder_transitions.basis: Width-only step. Capture rate held at 10%; corridor set expands from sourced flagships to the full mapped network.

ladder_transitions.headline: Network matures: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market + leading-operator capture
ladder_transitions.basis: Two-lever step. (1) Faster, more comfortable boats grow the cross-water market (induced demand). (2) Leading-operator capture lifts share from 10% floor to 25% mature, network-wide.

ladder_transitions.headline: Lens shift: Navier captured share → total inducible marine-transfer wallet
ladder_transitions.basis: Unit change. Divide SAM (the captured share) by leading-operator capture rate to recover the full inducible water-transfer market — the marine-mobility TAM.

ladder_transitions.headline: Marine transfer → total journey wallet (food, stays, experiences, in-app ads)
ladder_transitions.basis: Journey-wallet step. Each $1 of marine-transfer spend unlocks ~$3 of broader journey GMV across merchants the partner monetizes.

ladder_transitions.headline: Freenow platform take on Navier-carried journeys
ladder_transitions.basis: Platform-take step. Platform commission applied to the journey GMV routed through the Navier network (Navier-captured subset, not the full induced market).
